# brilliant-ble examples (Python)

<!-- Generated by tools/generate_example_indexes.py — edit the example docstrings/READMEs, not this file. -->

Examples for the low-level `brilliant-ble` BLE layer: sending Lua directly to the device REPL, uploading files, and device management. No message-layer protocol involved — see the `brilliant_msg` examples for the higher-level app pattern.

## Examples

| Example | Device-side Lua | Description |
|---|---|---|
| [`animated_drawing.py`](./animated_drawing.py) | `animated_drawing.lua` | Halo-only: upload and run a small animated drawing Lua app on the display. |
| [`callback_error.py`](./callback_error.py) |  | Show how Lua errors raised inside tap/data callbacks behave, and how to catch them with pcall. |
| [`custom_lua_functions.py`](./custom_lua_functions.py) | `fibonacci.lua` | Upload a Lua file of helper functions to the device and call them over BLE. |
| [`decompression.py`](./decompression.py) |  | Send compressed data to the device and decompress it on-device with frame.compression. |
| [`echo.py`](./echo.py) |  | Send Lua snippets to the device REPL and print the results (a tour of the Lua API over BLE). |
| [`halo_ancs_notifications.py`](./halo_ancs_notifications.py) | `ancs_notifications.lua` | Halo-only: install an iOS notification display app (ANCS). |
| [`halo_bitmap.py`](./halo_bitmap.py) |  | Halo-only: assign a custom display palette and draw indexed bitmaps with frame.display.bitmap(). |
| [`hello_noa.py`](./hello_noa.py) |  | Draw 'NOA' on the display, using a custom-palette bitmap on Halo and text on Frame. |
| [`hello_world.py`](./hello_world.py) |  | Print 'Hello' on the device display (Halo or Frame). |
| [`tap.py`](./tap.py) |  | Register a tap callback on the device and print a message each time it is tapped. |

## Device utilities

| Example | Device-side Lua | Description |
|---|---|---|
| [`clear_display.py`](./clear_display.py) |  | Clear the device display (blank the screen) on a Halo or Frame. |
| [`halo_fetch_logs.py`](./halo_fetch_logs.py) |  | Fetch the persisted /lfs log files from a Halo via the frame.log Lua API, then restart main.lua so the device returns to its normal app. |
| [`halo_standby.py`](./halo_standby.py) |  | Put a Halo into standby (low-power sleep), then disconnect. |
| [`ota_flash.py`](./ota_flash.py) |  | Flashes signed app firmware to a Halo device over the BLE SMP (MCUmgr) OTA service. |
| [`reset_palette.py`](./reset_palette.py) |  | Restore the device display colour palette to the firmware defaults (Halo or Frame). |
| [`send_break.py`](./send_break.py) |  | Send a break signal to stop any running Lua app so the device is ready for REPL commands. |
| [`send_remove.py`](./send_remove.py) |  | Halo-only: remove main.lua from the device so it stops auto-running an installed app. |
| [`send_reset.py`](./send_reset.py) |  | Soft-reset the device (restart the Lua VM). |
| [`stay_awake_false.py`](./stay_awake_false.py) |  | Restore normal sleep behaviour (device sleeps/turns off in the cradle) and put it to sleep now. |
| [`stay_awake_true.py`](./stay_awake_true.py) |  | Keep the device awake even in the charging cradle (useful during development). |
